images.caption: Figure 1:Comparison between the teacher agent (GPT-4.1) and the student agent (SFT-distilled Qwen3-1.7B) on a web information-retrieval task. The teacher maintains steady progress through coherent reasoning and actions(left), while the student suffers from progress stagnation, cycling through similar but ineffective search queries and remaining stuck(right).

images.caption: Figure 10:Qualitative comparison between SFT- and ProD-distilled Qwen3-1.7B student agents on a two-hop HotpotQA question. The SFT-distilled agent repeatedly issues similar search queries that attempt to jointly cover both hops, failing to extract useful intermediate information and exhibiting persistent progress stagnation(left). In contrast, the ProD-distilled agent decomposes the task into a clear two-hop search process, leveraging intermediate observations to guide subsequent actions and achieving steady progress toward the correct answer(right).

Figure 11:Qualitative comparison between SFT- and ProD-distilled Qwen3-4B student agents on a HotpotQA evaluation example. Although the SFT-distilled agent recognizes the failure of its initial search attempt, it remains trapped in a loop of near-duplicate queries without acquiring new information(left). By contrast, the ProD-distilled agent adapts its search strategy after early unsuccessful attempts, escapes the stagnation loop, and successfully retrieves the required information to solve the task(right).
